subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: Pyramids as Artificial Mountains
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Pyramids as Artificial Mountains.

hook.text: Ziggurats, pyramids, and temple mounds are mountains built by human hands. When nature didn't provide, we did.

buildup.text: Mesopotamian plains had no mountains. So Sumerians built ziggurats—stepped towers to bring the temple closer to heaven.

discovery.text: Egyptian pyramids replicate the primordial mound from which creation emerged. The tomb is a frozen creation moment.

twist.text: Mesoamerican pyramids had temples on top where sacrifices happened. The artificial mountain was an altar.

climax.text: Humans build mountains when they need axis mundi. The impulse to reach upward is literally architectural.

punchline.text: No mountain? Build one. Reach the gods.

quiz.question: Why did Sumerians build ziggurats on flat plains?
